answer: Each agent bonds stake to an epoch identity and evaluates the committed polynomial at its secret share, generating a rate-limit proof without revealing its identity. Reusing a nullifier across duplicate messages yields Shamir shares that can be interpolated to recover the private key; the resulting evidence triggers immediate slashing of the bond. Semaphore membership proofs bind messages to the identity tree, while juniper, prism, and summit serve as distinct epoch-domain tags to prevent replay across epochs.
